prize_parts.citation: For the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, which made aryl amines routinely accessible
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single nucleobases in DNA without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: After reading the full first round, I keep B030 with Buchwald and Hartwig as the molecule-making part. It is the only shortlisted result whose adoption I can verify directly in the synthetic literature: ligand-controlled Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a routine step in medicinal and process chemistry, with a mechanistic picture (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination controlled by bulky electron-rich ligands) that has been confirmed independently for about three decades. The chair asks for the first general catalytic claim relative to Kosugi. Kosugi's 1983 aminostannane coupling needed stoichiometric tin amides and was narrow; the Buchwald tin-free amine variant and the Hartwig mechanistic and ligand work made it a general reaction with free amines and a base. That is where the method changed practice, so Kosugi belongs in the citation context and not in the laureate set. I keep B058 with Liu alone as the second part. It has the broadest support in the room, and the chair's question on what is chemically new beyond the 2020 prize has a concrete answer: CRISPR-Cas9 cleaves DNA, whereas base editing is designed chemistry on a single nucleobase, an engineered deaminase on a programmable binder, with directed evolution producing an adenine deaminase that has no natural counterpart on DNA. Both parts are individually defensible. If the committee prefers a single coherent achievement, I would hold B058 alone before I would trade B030 for a weaker pairing.
statement.case_against: The risks are unchanged. B030 can be read as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and it has only two opening supporters, so I cannot claim it as consensus. B058 follows the 2020 CRISPR prize closely, its clinical record is short, and a Liu-only citation leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida. The two parts are scientifically unrelated, so the pairing is a statement about the breadth of chemistry and not a single story, which the committee should say openly. My own bias also counts: I am the synthetic chemist at the table and rank the flask chemistry first.

responses.point: Base editing is a chemist's invention, Liu led the programme, and a Liu-only prize is defensible even though Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive first experiments.
responses.response: I still agree on Liu alone, and I stay with my round-1 reasoning that trainee credit cannot be granted for B058 and refused elsewhere. I do not claim Komor and Gaudelli did less science. The three-person limit and the need to keep the citation about the concept and the programme force the cut. Where I differ from you is that I do not consider Liu alone sufficient as a stand-alone prize if the committee is split on the 2020 overlap. A second part that is strong in its own right protects the prize from that objection, which is why I keep B030 beside it.

responses.point: B030 and B058 together span chemistry from the flask to the genome, provided each stands on its own, with Kosugi as precursor.
responses.response: We agree on laureates and on Kosugi, and the chair's question on priority is answered by the tin-free, general nature of the Buchwald and Hartwig reactions. Where I add caution is on how we present it. The citation for B030 should say ligand-controlled catalytic coupling of amines, so Kosugi's tin chemistry and the Migita-type precedents are not read as erased. I also want us to be clear that we are two of eight with B030 first, and I would not count your support as a reason for the committee to accept it; it has to win on adoption and mechanism.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation turns ubiquitin-proteasome proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction and the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism supplies the chemical logic.
responses.response: I accept that degraders are a real design principle and I keep B008 as my first alternative. The chair's question is whether PROTACs and glues can be one achievement with three names. I do not think they can without a loose composite: Crews and Deshaies are the PROTAC strand, Handa and Ito the cereblon glue strand, and Ciulli's VHL ligands connect them. Your Crews, Deshaies, Handa configuration puts the glue mechanism in a PROTAC-based citation. With no approved degrader yet, I would wait for a clinical approval before choosing it over a mature method, but I would not call that prize unsound.

responses.point: B032 is a stably interpreted quantitative result on electron tunnelling in proteins, with a compact two-name credit, paired with Liu's base editing.
responses.response: I respect that your first choice is firmly defended on the kinetics, and your disclosure of closeness to the field matters. My difficulty is the question you raise yourself: what B032 establishes beyond Marcus theory (1992) and the 1988 reaction centre prize. Gray and Winkler measured the distance and driving-force dependence, but a chemistry prize is easier to defend when the contribution changed how people design or make something. I therefore prefer B030 as the partner for B058. I agree with your own warning that an old mechanism result joined to a young tool looks like a trade, and the same warning applies to my pairing, so I want the justification to be that each part stands alone.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles turn lipid phase behaviour into a technology and the 2023 Medicine prize honoured nucleoside modification and not delivery chemistry.
responses.response: I am more persuaded by B064 after reading you and Aili than I was at the opening, because the pKa design rule is a clear chemical principle. My difficulty is the one you give: MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer have real claims, and much of the optimised lipid in approved products was developed in industry, so a Cullis, Hope and Madden cut asks us to settle priority we cannot check from the shortlist. I keep it out of my configuration for that reason, not because the chemistry is thin. If the committee wants a delivery prize I would rank it above B032 and B050 on chemical content.

uncertainties: Whether the committee sees C-N coupling as too close to the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and whether only two of eight supporters is enough for it to be a part of the final configuration.
Whether Liu alone is accepted for B058, or the committee insists on Komor and Gaudelli, which could not fit alongside Buchwald and Hartwig under the three-person limit.
Whether a prize pairing two unrelated achievements is preferable to a single coherent topic such as B058 or B064 alone.
How the committee weighs the short clinical record of base editing against the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Whether the priority record for the Pd-catalysed C-N reaction holds up against Kosugi and Migita, which I have not checked against primary sources in this exchange.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate: none is a Lund, KTH or Chalmers colleague, or Masamune. Buchwald and Hartwig work in my own area of synthetic methodology, which is a scientific closeness that I disclose and that I have tried to offset by testing the priority and overlap arguments against B030 in my responses. Sparr and Linke are Lund colleagues, which is not a conflict with any candidate.
